display_name: AWS Bedrock Guardrails (cloud-native, wrapped by LiteLLM)
install_tell: AWS-managed service on bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com; SigV4 OR AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK bearer token. Caller addresses a specific guardrailIdentifier + guardrailVersion provisioned in the customer's AWS account.
misconfig_patterns: guardrailIdentifier leakage: the identifier is not a secret per se, but pairs with leaked AWS creds for direct abuse. Verify-do-not-exercise.
AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK in LiteLLM config / .env on a public box: short-lived bearer that bypasses SigV4 signing. If exposed, grants direct ApplyGuardrail invoke quota until rotation.

Operators sometimes proxy LiteLLM Bedrock guardrails through the LiteLLM proxy at :4000 to centralize keys; this means CVE-2026-40217 (LiteLLM custom-code guardrail sandbox escape) and the Cat-05 LiteLLM CVE chain become reachable upstream of the cloud-native guardrail.
Disabled-by-default: the guardrail must be CONFIGURED with policy; an unconfigured guardrail returns NONE intervention. Operators sometimes ship 'guardrail enabled' with empty policy.

active_probe.false_positive_check: All AWS endpoints answer; identity is in SigV4 response, not status code. Not a discoverable surface from Shodan; lives in operator config files, not on the wire.

shodan_dorks.basic: n/a - AWS shared infrastructure, no operator-distinguishable fingerprint at the cloud edge

deployment_tells: guardrailIdentifier + guardrailVersion appear in LiteLLM YAML config and in customer Bedrock console
AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK or AWS SigV4 in Authorization header
pivot_paths: Leaked guardrailIdentifier in client SPA bundles or public GitHub configs is a content/policy disclosure, not direct access; pair with leaked AWS creds for invoke.
LiteLLM proxy that wraps Bedrock guardrails inherits the LiteLLM CVE chain (CVE-2026-40217, CVE-2026-49468, CVE-2026-42208, CVE-2026-42203). The wrapper IS the new attack surface.

added_surface: LiteLLM-side credential storage (AWS keys land in proxy .env or DB).
LiteLLM /guardrails/* endpoints expose guardrail name + presence to anyone with proxy read.
LiteLLM custom-code guardrail CVE-2026-40217 lives in the same hook namespace; any operator running Bedrock guardrails via LiteLLM is one config line away from also enabling the vulnerable hook.
LiteLLM adds masking helpers (_redact_pii_matches) that re-process Bedrock JSON before returning to caller; an LiteLLM bug here would alter the apparent guardrail decision.
litellm_wrapper_delta.verdict: NOT a transparent passthrough. LiteLLM adds credential surface, a control-plane endpoint, and an upstream wrapper subject to its own CVE chain. The cloud-native guardrail itself is unchanged; the operator's blast radius widens.

disclosure_contact.channel_observed: aws-security@amazon.com (cloud vendor disclosure; not the channel for LiteLLM-side wrapper bugs)
